title: Korean alphabet introduction
culture: Hangul letters form syllable blocks. A block is not always a whole word.

quiz.question: What is 한글?
quiz.explanation: 한글 — Korean alphabet. Hangul letters form syllable blocks. A block is not always a whole word.

title: Basic vowels
culture: Start with ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ. Romanization is only a guide.

quiz.question: Match the vowel sound: 아
quiz.explanation: 아 — a vowel sound. Start with ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ. Romanization is only a guide.

title: Basic consonants
culture: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ are basic consonants. Use polite speech with unfamiliar adults.

quiz.question: Listen and select the syllable you hear.
quiz.explanation: 나 — I / me (informal). ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ are basic consonants. Use polite speech with unfamiliar adults.

title: Combining letters
culture: ㄱ + ㅏ combine into 가. Syllables begin with a consonant letter.

quiz.question: Complete: ㄱ + ㅏ = ___
quiz.explanation: 가 — the syllable ga. ㄱ + ㅏ combine into 가. Syllables begin with a consonant letter.

title: Reading simple syllables
culture: A bottom consonant is called 받침. 학교 contains two syllable blocks.

quiz.question: Translate 학교 into English.
quiz.explanation: 학교 — school. A bottom consonant is called 받침. 학교 contains two syllable blocks.

title: Basic pronunciation
culture: Final consonants may sound different when followed by another syllable. Listen to native pronunciation.

quiz.question: What does 한국 mean?
quiz.explanation: 한국 — Korea. Final consonants may sound different when followed by another syllable. Listen to native pronunciation.

title: Greetings
culture: 안녕하세요 is a common polite greeting. A small bow is often natural.

quiz.question: Arrange the Korean greeting to a teacher.
quiz.explanation: 안녕하세요 — hello. 안녕하세요 is a common polite greeting. A small bow is often natural.

title: Introducing yourself
culture: 저 is a polite way to refer to yourself. 이에요 follows a noun ending in a consonant.

quiz.question: What does 학생 mean?
quiz.explanation: 학생 — student. 저 is a polite way to refer to yourself. 이에요 follows a noun ending in a consonant.

title: Numbers
culture: Korean has Sino-Korean and native Korean number systems. Usage depends on context.

quiz.question: Complete the Sino-Korean sequence: 일, 이, ___
quiz.explanation: 일 — one (Sino-Korean). Korean has Sino-Korean and native Korean number systems. Usage depends on context.

title: Everyday expressions
culture: 감사합니다 is polite and appropriate in many everyday situations.

quiz.question: Translate 감사합니다 into English.
quiz.explanation: 감사합니다 — thank you. 감사합니다 is polite and appropriate in many everyday situations.

title: At the university
culture: 어디예요? politely asks where something is.

quiz.question: What is 도서관?
quiz.explanation: 도서관 — library. 어디예요? politely asks where something is.

title: At immigration
culture: Use the Korean term 예약 when discussing appointments. This is a language lesson, not procedural guidance.

quiz.question: What does 예약 mean?
quiz.explanation: 예약 — reservation / appointment. Use the Korean term 예약 when discussing appointments. This is a language lesson, not procedural guidance.
